title and abstract.summary: The study evaluated the relationship between various functional traits (body size, phenology, nesting location, sociality, and foraging choice) and the prevalence of three pathogens (trypanosomes, neogregarines, and Nosema ceranae) across wild bee communities, and also examined intra-specific size variation in Bombus impatiens. The study discusses how various functional traits in bees, such as body size and phenology, might influence pathogen prevalence and disease dynamics within bee communities, using Bombus impatiens as an example.
